blockers.title: The supposedly folded trigger table remains an explicit selector-decision authority and custody input
blockers.subjectEvidence: authority says the ownership record is the only impact authority and 'There is no separate uncustodied trigger table.' Step 6 uses ownershipRecord.sharedSurfaceConsumers. But selectorDecision still derives perLaneExplanation from 'ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and ambiguityPolicy' and inputsDigest still covers 'ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and change set'. ID-DEP-C6 likewise still names 'Ownership-record / trigger-table / dependency-edge custody bytes'.
blockers.counterexample: An implementation can follow the selectorDecision contract and supply a separate trigger table whose omitted publisher/surface edge suppresses a shared lane. None of sharedSurfaceConsumers' custody/completeness rules necessarily governs those separate bytes, exactly recreating CLAUDE-V2-B2. If it instead follows authority and supplies no table, it cannot construct the required selectorDecision digest/explanation as written.
blockers.whyBlocking: The output evidence is the auditable account of why lanes ran or skipped. It cannot simultaneously prove a one-authority algorithm and require an independently named second authority. The unchanged ID-DEP-C6 confirms this is not merely one stray prose token. The claimed fold is therefore false at load-bearing selector paths.
blockers.requiredRepair: Remove the separate trigger-table concept everywhere: replace both selectorDecision references with ownershipRecord.sharedSurfaceConsumers under the single ownership-record digest, and amend ID-DEP-C6 to name the folded consumer relation rather than trigger-table bytes. If a distinct table is actually intended, restore it honestly with its own custody, completeness, self-change, ambiguity, and mutation-test contract. Roster the ID-DEP-C6 change in the successor delta.

blockers.title: G16-3 still accepts SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE for an out-of-universe owner that v3 makes REFUSE-only
blockers.subjectEvidence: C-CONFLICT-OWNER covers either more than one owner or an owner outside the universe. G16-3 says C-MISSING-OWNER and C-CONFLICT-OWNER may produce REFUSE or SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE. The repaired ambiguity law instead says SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE is unlawful when universe construction is invalid or an ownerId/component declaration is missing; comparisonBasis says the only lawful action then is REFUSE.
blockers.counterexample: Feed the hostile G16 corpus a changed unit whose ownerId names an undeclared component outside the comparison-basis universe. The harness may choose SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE and pass G16-3's stated alternatives, even though the unknown component lane cannot be in that universe and both repaired selector laws require REFUSE.
blockers.whyBlocking: The implementation law is repaired but the acceptance class still blesses the exact unsafe result the repair forbids. A future harness can therefore qualify conformance to G16-3 while violating fail-safe and omitting the affected lane. This leaves CLAUDE-V2-S2/CODEX-V2-B1 unresolved at the test boundary.
blockers.requiredRepair: Split the hostile cases and their expected outcomes. Missing/out-of-universe owner, missing component declaration, or incomplete universe construction must require REFUSE only. Multiple/conflicting owners may allow SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE only after the comparison-basis universe is independently complete and valid. Add exact corpus assertions for both branches.
